result.title: Digital Prosthetic Customization: A Dual Perspective Analysis
result.summary: Digital prosthetic customisation platforms operate as asymmetric collaboration spaces that concentrate configurative authority and decision-making responsibility with technical professionals in socket design contexts while granting end users meaningful but supervised agency in control customisation contexts, with automation functioning throughout as a cognitive offload mechanism that encodes clinical expertise rather than replacing it—and the field's central gap is the near-absence of direct evidence for upper-limb socket design platforms, leaving the transferability of well-developed lower-limb paradigms unvalidated.
